oracle: CEN/TC 434 eInvoicing EN 16931 validation artefacts, release 1.3.17, run in process

corpus.note: The four are recorded instance by instance in corpus.md and in ../syntax/ledger.json; the artefacts raise the same rule on the same instance with the flag fatal, and the profile of each document levels that finding down to information.

causes.artefact-cannot-fire: The artefact's expression for the rule cannot report anything on any document. The pack follows the norm: it faults what the norm faults and warns inside the zone the artefact of the other syntax grants.
causes.artefact-drops-a-prefix: Release 1.3.17 dropped EL from the prefixes BR-CO-09 admits, in both artefacts, while the standard admits EL for Greece in the statement of the rule itself. The pack follows the standard: a VAT identifier with the prefix EL passes here and is reported by the artefacts.
causes.artefact-reads-the-norm-narrowly: The artefact's expression is narrower than the statement of the standard, and the pack follows the standard. Each case is named in ledger.md with both readings.
causes.artefact-reports-an-absent-identifier: The UBL artefact of release 1.3.17 reports BR-CO-09 on a VAT tax scheme that states no identifier: it tests the first two characters of an identifier that is not there. The standard asks the prefix of a VAT identifier that is stated, and the pack reports nothing where none is. Release 1.3.16 passed the same documents. The mutations that show it remove BT-31, BT-32 or BT-63 and leave the tax scheme element they stood in.
causes.artefact-swaps-two-families: The CII artefact of release 1.3.17 gives the identifiers BR-IG-* to the rules of the VAT category M and BR-IP-* to those of the category L, the other way round from the standard and from the UBL artefact of the same release, and its rules of the category L ask for a rate greater than zero where the standard asks for zero or greater. The pack follows the standard: BR-IG-* is the category L, and zero is a rate it admits. A CII mutation of either family is reported by the artefact under the identifiers of the other.
causes.artefacts-disagree-on-a-tolerance: The two official artefacts of release 1.3.17 do not read the rule the same way: one of them accepts a stated amount within one unit of the invoice currency of the figure it is compared with and the other asks for equality, or the two draw the boundary of that unit in different places. The pack faults what both artefacts fault and reports a warning, which decides no verdict, inside the zone only one of them grants, naming the syntax whose artefact faults the figure there. conformance/rules/ledger.md carries the matrix.
causes.artefacts-not-chosen: The mutation is about the specification identifier (BT-24), which is the term the syntax engine chooses the artefacts by. Without it no rule set is run at all, so the official side of the comparison is empty by construction.
causes.category-bound-differently: The artefacts number the rules of the not subject to VAT category after the element each syntax writes, so the two artefacts report different identifiers for the same defect and this engine, which is a statement about business terms, can follow only one of them.
causes.not-in-the-release: The rule is one this pack carries and release 1.3.17 does not, so the official side has nothing to say about it.
causes.notation-lost-on-import: The source wrote an amount with more fraction digits than the type admits and the digits beyond it were zeros. The canonical decimal form does not carry them, so after the import the number is the same number written shorter and the decimal rule has no over-scale left to see. The artefacts read the lexical form of the XML and report.
causes.operand-removed: The mutation removes a business term that other rules compute with. The artefacts' expression compares against what is not there and reports those rules as well; this engine reports the missing term and leaves a rule whose operand is absent undecided.
causes.term-lost-on-import: The syntax binding did not carry the business term the rule is about into the semantic document. Either this engine has nothing to decide where the artefacts do, or it decides a rule against an operand that is absent only because of the import. The cause is named in conformance/rules/not-applicable.md with the element that was lost.

tolerances.note: How closely release 1.3.17 asks the two figures of a rule to agree, read out of the vendored artefacts by ToleranceMatrixTest. The pack faults from the wider of the two readings on and warns inside the zone only one artefact grants, naming in warns the syntax whose artefact faults a figure there; canFire false says that the assertion of the strict reading cannot report on any document, and warns is then none, because nothing faults a figure inside that zone and the warning states what the standard asks. ledger.md has the matrix and names the mutations that measure the zone, its edges and what lies beyond.

timings.taken: 2026-09-20, one machine, Java 21, best of three evaluations of a warmed virtual machine, as recorded in ledger.md
